title: Pipes and stderr
hints: The child reads standard input until it ends, and stdin only ends when the pipe is closed. Nobody closes it, so the child waits forever, until ctx kills it.
Close stdin after writing the input. Simpler still: skip StdinPipe and set cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(input).
Capture standard error in its own bytes.Buffer (cmd.Stderr = &errBuf) and include its trimmed text in the error you return when the command fails.
